hypotheses.justification: Only `p` and the argument `b` occur in the statement; `ℓ`, `A`, `[Fact ℓ.Prime]` and `[CharP (ResidueField ↥A) ℓ]` are not arguments (their types mention section variables that are not used, so Lean does not include them). `[NeZero p]` however is included: it is instance-implicit and the only section variable in its type, `p`, is an argument (this is exactly the automatic-inclusion rule implemented in `Lean.Elab.MutualDef.withHeaderSecVars`, and the reason `Definitions/Def_ModularCurve_X0.lean` needs `omit [NeZero N] in` on lemmas that don't use the instance). It is not needed: `modularFunctionFieldFull` (Definitions/Def_ModularCurve_X0.lean:305) is a `def` whose type is `IntermediateField ℚ (LaurentSeries ℚ)` and whose value only mentions `N` (via `divisorExpansions N`, whose own body, `∃ (d : ℕ) (_ : NeZero d), d ∣ N ∧ x = qExpand ℚ d jq`, does not use the section instance either), so by `Meta.removeUnused` a def only takes the section variables occurring in its type/value — `modularFunctionFieldFull p` therefore needs no `NeZero p` instance. Likewise `laurentBaseChange` (Def_ModularCurve_LaurentCoeff.lean:103), `coeffEmb` and the `abbrev bar` (line 379, whose body uses only `p` and `b`) take no such instance. Hence the statement elaborates unchanged after deleting the argument, and the proof is still literally `rfl` (`Eq.refl` of `coeffEmb (AlgebraicClosure ℚ) (b : LaurentSeries ℚ)`, definitionally equal to the coercion of the subtype pair `⟨coeffEmb … , _⟩`). So `omit [NeZero p] in theorem coe_bar ... := rfl` works; the `[NeZero p]` argument is unused both in the type and in the proof. No other argument can be deleted: `p` and `b` both occur in the statement.
